findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body:
`fetch_error_details` takes `timestamp` from the nodestore event payload, which is float seconds since epoch (~1.7e9). `gen_request_data` compares it against the top-level `timestamp` of replay recording events (lines 153-155). The JS SDK writes those in milliseconds (`breadcrumb.timestamp * 1000`, ~1.7e12).

With real data every error looks earlier than every breadcrumb. All errors are emitted at the start of the log instead of being interleaved chronologically, which is the main point of this change. The emitted messages also mix units (`at 1.7e9` for errors, `at 1.7e12` for breadcrumbs), which misleads the LLM.

The tests hide this because they use seconds for both. Convert the error timestamp to milliseconds (`* 1000`) before sorting and comparing, and use ms in the tests.

findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes nodestore get_multi preserves input order
findings.body:
`nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node_id. Its order is not guaranteed to match `error_ids`: cached items come first, then fetched ones, and missing entries may be omitted entirely. Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` can therefore attach the wrong event id to each payload, or shift every id after a missing one.

Look up each payload by its generated node_id instead, e.g. `events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, event_id))`.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only hidden while a search query is entered
findings.body:
The memo returns `sorted` unfiltered when `searchQuery` is empty. The `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` check only runs in the search branch.

In the default view (no search) `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are still shown. They disappear only once the user types something, which is inconsistent and almost certainly not intended. Filter out hidden attributes before the early return.

findings.title: Mutual-exclusion check for age/timestamp uses truthiness
findings.body:
`validate_timestamp` checks `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `validate_age` checks `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. A legitimate value of 0 is falsy, so a report carrying both `timestamp` and `age: 0` passes validation even though the fields are meant to be mutually exclusive. `age` is in milliseconds, so 0 is realistic.

Nothing requires at least one of the two to be present either, despite the docstrings. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` / `"timestamp" in self.initial_data`, and add a `validate()` that requires exactly one.

findings.title: One invalid report rejects the whole batch, so valid reports are dropped and retried
findings.body:
The endpoint returns 422 as soon as any report in the array fails validation, for example an unlisted or new report type in the strict `ChoiceField`. Per the Reporting API, any non-2xx response marks delivery as failed, and the browser retries the entire batch.

As a result, the valid reports in that batch are never counted, and the same payload is re-sent repeatedly. Consider counting the valid reports and logging or skipping the invalid ones instead of failing the request.

findings.title: No remaining test exercises the application/reports+json content type
findings.body:
The removed `test_logs_request_data_if_option_enabled` and the old multiple-reports test were the only tests that posted with `content_type="application/reports+json"`. Every test now uses the default JSON format.

The custom `BrowserReportsJSONParser` is the content type real browsers send, and it is no longer covered. A regression in parser registration would go unnoticed. Keep at least one success-path test using that media type.

findings.title: Data migrations turned into no-ops pointing to a migration not included in this PR
findings.body:
Both 0917 and 0920 now just `return` and point readers to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`. That migration is not added in this PR, and the migrations lockfile is unchanged.

If 0921 does not already exist, organization-visible saved searches are never converted to GroupSearchViews. This affects every environment that has not run these migrations yet, including self-hosted. The comment would also be a dangling reference. Either include the replacement migration or confirm it exists.

findings.title: Feature-flagged TableWidgetVisualization always renders an empty table
findings.body:
When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, the widget renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and hard-coded empty `tableData`. It ignores `result.data`, `result.meta`, the loading state and the field aliases.

Any org with the flag on sees empty table widgets on every dashboard, with no loading indicator. Map `result` into `TabularData` and columns before gating real users onto this flag.

findings.title: Query key omits organization, allowing cached attributes to leak across orgs
findings.body:
The new react-query key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`. `queryOptions` contains item type, attribute type, project ids and datetime, but not the organization slug, while the queryFn fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/...`.

When switching organizations with the same page filters (e.g. `projects: []` for "My Projects" and the same period), the cached attribute keys from the previous org are served until the refetch completes.

This refactor also dropped the previous `retry: false` / `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so failures now retry with backoff by default. Include `organization.slug` in the key and restore the intended query options.

findings.title: Container lost align-items and gap during Flex migration
findings.body:
The removed `Container` was `styled(FlexBox)`, so it had `align-items: center` and `gap: space(1)` in addition to `justify-content: space-between`. The replacement `<Flex ref={setRef} justify="space-between">` sets only the justify.

The tabs and `TraceContextVitals` are no longer vertically centered and have no gap between them, which is a visual regression from what was meant to be a no-op refactor. Add `align="center" gap={space(1)}`.
